newsitem.title: LEBANON: Opposition gathering blasts Lebanon media law.
newsitem.headline: Opposition gathering blasts Lebanon media law.

text.p: About 2,500 Lebanese protesters took part in a weekend gathering near Beirut to protest a government decision to ban dozens of private television and radio stations.

Citizens, media workers, unionists, parliamentary deputies and political party representatives took part in the meeting held on Saturday and Sunday at a convent in the coastal town of Antelias, 10 km (six miles) north of Beirut.

They demanded the cancellation of a new law under which the government ordered dozens of Lebanon's many private radio and television stations to close by November 30 and licensed only a handful of stations mostly owned by officials.
Live performance of local popular singers and musicians attracted hundreds of Lebanese families to the gathering where they signed a huge petition "vowing to defend rights and liberties in Lebanon".
Inside the convent, the participants issued a statement on Sunday "calling for the cancellation of decisions taken under the media organisational law".
Under the September law, which has sparked sit-ins and strike threats, the government licensed only four television and 11 radio stations out of a total on nearly 200.

Three of the licenced television stations are owned by prominent government figures, including Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri -- reappointed last week for a third term --, while two of the three radio stations allowed to broadcast news bulletins are owned by the same politicians.

The statement also called for the formation of an independent body to replace the government-appointed National Council for Audiovisual Media and said the new council "should have the jurisdiction to license television and radio stations".
The current audiovisual council is a consultative body whose decisions are not binding to the government but it had recommended the ban.
